La Pinsonniere was unlucky at Newbury to be beaten half a length, despite being badly hampered by a faller at the second. The step up in class is unlikely to be a barrier to success.

The Frankel colt, a half-brother to the classy Siskin who was arguably a better three-year-old than he was a juvenile, might not be of a similar echelon, but an opening mark of 84 looks workable and he could step forward now. Yabher was unsuited by testing conditions at Haydock when last seen but he ought to fare better on better ground, while Hugo Palmer, who sprung a surprise to win this 12 months ago with a 33/1 shot , looks to have a solid chance with King Casper.

The latter reopposes on slightly better terms with Ryan Moore taking over the reins and may well turn the tables. selections.comment: A 6lb penalty may not be enough to stop GREEN PURSUIT landing a quick-fire double having sluiced in on season debut last week. He took a big step forward on last term's level and gave the impression there's more in the locker. Lord Roxby and American Style look best placed to take advantage of any faltering by the selection with the former edging it despite flopping on nursery handicap debut on his final outing last year. Eased back a grade and back at 6f, which looked to suit on career debut before his sole victory over a stiff 5f, he looks on a very workable mark given his novice/maiden form. American Style is perhaps less likely to be near peak fitness but is a threat based on the form of his final two outings last term when winning as maiden before finsishing midfield in the ultra-competitive Listed 2YO Trophy at Redcar.

selections.comment: BOWOOD took big strides forward last year being raised 20lb, a streak that included a hat-trick on the turf, one of which was a convincing CD win, and Ivan Furtodo's charge looks to be the most reliable in a trappy event. Much will depend on the fitness of some of those returning off a layoff. Garden Oasis is one and would be a solid option if his fitness could be taken on trust but he's tended to need a pipe-opener and is overlooked this time. Top weight On The River has a better record fresh and while looking handicapped to the hilt for now can still make his presence felt on a track that suits well. Overnight Oasis is fit and a threat on the pick of his form but has to bounce back from a poor effort last time when raised to this class. So, Pisanello is taken to chase home the selection. David O'Meara's gelding can go well fresh and is versatile ground-wise. While he lost form late last term it's hoped the break might have freshend him up and he's on a dangeropus mark if rediscovering some verve.
